findings.highlight: My chest hurts
findings.evidenceJa: 肺が苦しい
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s lungs are laboring painfully.
findings.explanation: The English relocates respiratory distress into generic chest pain.

findings.highlight: My heart
findings.evidenceJa: 胸の上から押さえつけた心臓
findings.governingReading: Sakura presses down on her heart through her chest.
findings.explanation: The English omits her physical attempt to restrain it.

findings.highlight: sending me a danger signal for a while now
findings.evidenceJa: ずいぶん前から慌ただしく危険信号
findings.governingReading: Her heart has frantically signaled danger since long before this moment.
findings.explanation: The English weakens both the long duration and frantic manner.

findings.highlight: as though saying it’ll [block len=3] if it moves anymore
findings.evidenceJa: 何より先にワシが死ぬわ、と抗議する
findings.governingReading: Her heart comically protests in an elderly first-person voice that it will die before anything else.
findings.explanation: The English loses the elderly “washi” voice and the claim that the heart dies first.

findings.highlight: swallowing needles
findings.evidenceJa: トゲを飲み下すよう
findings.governingReading: Each breath feels like swallowing thorns.
findings.explanation: The English changes the organic tearing image to needles.

findings.highlight: I might fall unconscious at any time
findings.evidenceJa: いつ倒れてもおかしくはない
findings.governingReading: Sakura could physically collapse at any moment.
findings.explanation: The English specifies unconsciousness, which the line does not establish.

findings.highlight: I need to
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女[line3]わたしはここで
findings.governingReading: The narration pivots from “she” into Sakura’s first-person “I” as resolve returns.
findings.explanation: The English omits the focalization shift.

findings.highlight: I need to settle my match
findings.evidenceJa: 自分に決着をつけなくてはいけない
findings.governingReading: Sakura must settle matters with herself.
findings.explanation: The English turns this into a malformed match and omits its object.

findings.highlight: stop the old man that made me a Master, even if it costs me my life
findings.evidenceJa: 刺し違えてでも止めなくてはいけない
findings.governingReading: Sakura resolves to stop Zouken even if she must strike him down while dying herself.
findings.explanation: The English retains her death but omits the required mutual destruction of Zouken.

findings.highlight: look at him, like I do every night at dinner
findings.evidenceJa: 食事時のように顔を合わせて
findings.governingReading: Sakura imagines facing Zouken as ordinarily as at mealtime.
findings.explanation: The English invents a nightly shared-dinner routine.

findings.highlight: that old man’s scheme will end
findings.evidenceJa: とりあえずは、あの老人の企みは全て終わる
findings.governingReading: Her refusal would, provisionally, end all of Zouken’s schemes.
findings.explanation: The English drops both the provisional limit and the totality of his plans.

findings.highlight: after I disobey the monster
findings.evidenceJa: あの妖怪を拒絶した自分
findings.governingReading: Sakura refuses or rejects the monstrous old man.
findings.explanation: The English frames the act as disobedience, preserving his authority over her.

findings.highlight: It’s damp, degenerate, and viscous like always
findings.evidenceJa: いつも通り陰湿で、退廃で、粘質
findings.governingReading: The house is as insidious or oppressive, decadent, and clinging as ever.
findings.explanation: The English mistakes 陰湿 for literal dampness and leaves the description unnatural.

findings.highlight: wants me back
findings.evidenceJa: わたしを回収したがっていた
findings.governingReading: Sakura believes Zouken wanted to retrieve or collect her as the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English reduces instrumental collection to wanting her back.

findings.highlight: he couldn’t do anything until now because I was at the Emiya household
findings.evidenceJa: 手を出せなくて、今まで手をこまねいていたんだと思う
findings.governingReading: Sakura had thought the Emiya house prevented Zouken from acting and left him waiting helplessly.
findings.explanation: The English removes attribution to her belief and states his inability as fact.

findings.highlight: how far I run
findings.evidenceJa: どんなに遠くにいても
findings.governingReading: Zouken can find Sakura however far away she is.
findings.explanation: The English adds flight or running to a statement about distance.

findings.highlight: the possibility that I might resist
findings.evidenceJa: たとえわたしに逆らう意思があるとしても
findings.governingReading: Even if Sakura has an actual intention to resist, Zouken will not account for it.
findings.explanation: The English turns her existing will into a mere possibility.

findings.highlight: He only treats me as a tool
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで通り、わたしを道具として扱うだけ
findings.governingReading: Zouken will treat Sakura as a tool just as he always has.
findings.explanation: The English retains instrumentality but omits the long coercive history.

findings.highlight: removed some of my crest worm
findings.evidenceJa: 体内の刻印虫が減って
findings.governingReading: Kirei’s treatment reduced the crest worms inside Sakura’s body.
findings.explanation: The English uses an ungrammatical mass singular and changes reduction into removal.

findings.highlight: He knows
findings.evidenceJa: さっきから知っている
findings.governingReading: Zouken has known for some time that Sakura came alone after leaving Rider behind.
findings.explanation: The English omits the duration of his awareness.
